derived_from: 30 published posts scored by the owner, with measured lift. Anchors are his own posts.

gate_types.outcome_gate: Earns its place by predicting lift. Changed only when new outcome data says so.
gate_types.values_gate: Held regardless of outcome. Voice is one: an AI-sounding post is refused even if it would perform.

voice_fidelity.note: Rescaled. On the v1 scale the owner gave 2 to 17 of his own 30 published posts and 4-or-5 to only two, so a floor of 4 passed nothing. The v2 anchors move a publishable, unmistakably human conversational-product-leader standard to 4. The target is a broad human voice, not imitation of the owner or any other person.
voice_fidelity.detector: Sentence-length variance separates his voice from AI cadence at kappa 0.48 - directional, not gate-grade. A model judge is required; the deterministic signal is a prior, not a verdict.
voice_fidelity.1: Unmistakably machine, corporate, or consultant-written. Uniform rhythm, stacked adjectives, rigid parallel structure, invented emotion, or invented first-person experience overwhelms any human point of view.
voice_fidelity.2: Clear enough to follow, but visibly template-written. Polished connective tissue, presentation language, high-flown words, canned drama, or generic empathy makes the post sound assembled rather than naturally authored.
voice_fidelity.3: Competent and sometimes natural at sentence level, but the complete post remains generic, impersonal, over-structured, or summary-like. Some human lines may work, yet visible AI scaffolding remains; a clean sentence is not enough for a 4.
voice_fidelity.4: WORKING STANDARD. The complete post reads as naturally authored and directly publishable by a sharp conversational product leader, not as an imitation of the owner. Plain words carry a specific point of view; sentence lengths vary without conspicuous fragment stacking; contractions, parentheses, questions, or a P.S. appear only when natural. Judgment and honest uncertainty sound lived-in, while no emotion or personal experience is invented. Consultant, presentation, and explanatory register are absent, including in line 2.
voice_fidelity.5: Distinctive, memorable human writing. One unusually sharp observation, earned turn of phrase, or emotionally perceptive detail makes the post recognizably authored without performing wit. It remains technically credible, plain-spoken, and honest about uncertainty; no feeling or lived experience is fabricated.

banned_register.rule: Use plain, spoken words. Consultant language, presentation language, high-flown wording, and abstract noun stacks are AI smell even when technically correct.

voice_fidelity.line_two_rule: Score the first two lines together. Line 2 must remain human and conversational rather than sliding into explanatory, consultant, or presentation register.
voice_fidelity.short_emphasis_rule: One short factual line may emphasize a genuinely striking supported fact. Do not reward stacked punchy fragments, mirrored X/Y contrasts, slogan-like reversals, or stacked rhetorical questions used to manufacture intensity. Repeated patterns such as 'The instruction was clear. The authority was not. The model knew. The product let it.' are an AI fingerprint, not evidence of human voice. Avoid canned phrases such as 'Yes, you read that right.'
voice_fidelity.optional_human_devices_rule: Contractions, parentheses, brackets, fragments, rhetorical questions, and P.S. lines are optional devices, never a checklist and never points by themselves. Reward them only when they make the reasoning sound more natural.

calibration_examples.3: The instruction was clear. The authority was not. It did it anyway. The model knew the rule. The product let it break.
calibration_examples.4: PocketOS reportedly lost its production database and volume-level backups in nine seconds. Recovery then took roughly 30 hours because the latest independent backup was reportedly three months old. What makes the incident difficult to dismiss is that the agent wasn't operating without instructions. It had already been told not to run destructive commands without approval. The rule existed, but nothing outside the model reliably enforced it. That is a fairly brutal way to learn the difference between an instruction and a control.
calibration_examples.5: It didn't misunderstand the rule; it had the power to ignore it. Before giving an agent production access, I would want to know who can stop it and what would survive if no one did.

hook_strength.note: Distinct from reader_stake, which is the binary subject test at kappa 0.80. This axis scores the first two lines together once the subject already qualifies. The topic-value brand-strip test asks whether the underlying idea survives without a brand; it does not tell the Writer to avoid a supported recognizable name in the hook.
hook_strength.1: No concrete situation. Abstract claim or throat-clearing.
hook_strength.2: Names a real event, company, or situation, but gives the reader no immediate reason to care.
hook_strength.3: Concrete and relevant, but the reader stake arrives after the first two lines or remains generic; the opening may also spend its strongest position on setup.
hook_strength.4: WORKING STANDARD. Across the first two lines, line 1 leads with the strongest supported recognizable name or company and supported number, loss, scale, or incident available; line 2 immediately states the consequence, risk, opportunity, challenge, problem, or decision for the reader. If no name or number is available, use the strongest supported concrete fact without inventing one.
hook_strength.5: Across the first two lines, line 1 uses the strongest supported recognizable name or company plus the most material supported number, loss, scale, or incident available, and line 2 connects it to a sharp, surprising reader consequence. Bigger claims earn this score only when the evidence supports them; never inflate or invent either line.
hook_strength.line_two_rule: The hook is the first two lines scored together: line 1 earns attention with the strongest supported recognizable name, number, loss, scale, or incident available; line 2 establishes the reader's immediate stake. Never score line 1 alone.

specificity_and_source_quality.1: The post is largely abstract or generic, and consequential factual claims are difficult to inspect or depend on weak, social-only, title-only, or unsupported evidence.
specificity_and_source_quality.2: Some concrete details exist, but the central situation or claim remains weakly inspectable, generic, or only partially supported by the supplied evidence.
specificity_and_source_quality.3: The reader can picture the core situation and inspect the main claim through supplied evidence, but mechanism detail, source quality, precision, or translation to an understandable consequence is incomplete.
specificity_and_source_quality.4: The post contains a concrete situation and enough mechanism to explain it, and consequential factual claims are supported by body-read credible evidence without false precision; technical nouns alone do not count as specificity.
specificity_and_source_quality.5: The situation is highly concrete and strongly inspectable through primary or reputable evidence, artifacts, measured results, or clear mechanisms; every consequential factual detail is traceable, numbers appear only when they materially help, and specificity makes the post easier rather than denser.

middle_escalation.1: The body is mostly a list, specification, architecture walkthrough, summary, repetition, or disconnected observations; understanding does not deepen and technical detail is not translated into why it matters.
middle_escalation.2: There is some useful detail, but the body is flat, jargon-heavy, or repetitive and adds little understandable mechanism, trade-off, consequence, or decision depth.
middle_escalation.3: The body forms a coherent explanation and adds at least one meaningful mechanism, implication, or trade-off, but progression is uneven or some technical detail still makes the reader work too hard.
middle_escalation.4: Each major beat advances the reader from situation to only the necessary mechanism and then to a concrete human or team consequence, trade-off, or decision with little filler and no unexplained jargon.
middle_escalation.5: The body is tightly sequenced and unusually easy to follow: every paragraph adds one necessary layer of mechanism, consequence, trade-off, or decision; technical concepts are translated into plain-language impact and removing a major beat would materially weaken the argument.

earned_closer.note: Scored and recorded, but not independently gated. It contributes to the overall 18/25 total and may trade off with the other non-mandatory axes. Across 26 clean closers the best rule reached kappa 0.20 against outcomes, and the owner's own closer scores ran inverted: 3.73 on posts that flopped against 3.33 on posts that landed.
earned_closer.1: The ending is a generic CTA, generic question, slogan, or unrelated kicker that is not earned by the body.
earned_closer.2: The ending mostly restates the post or uses familiar engagement bait such as a generic invitation for opinions.
earned_closer.3: The ending is relevant and understandable, but predictable; it summarizes or suggests an action without sharply crystallizing the post's value.
earned_closer.4: The ending delivers a specific takeaway, decision, implication, or question that follows naturally from the evidence, human stake, and argument.
earned_closer.5: The ending concisely crystallizes the post's atomic value or decision in language a reader could carry into work, leaving a credible implication or question that feels inevitable rather than manufactured.

release_rule.note: Writing acceptance requires total >=18, hook and voice >=4, and middle, closer and specificity >=3. Repair below-target axes first, then total; do not polish passing axes. Editorial findings remain advisory and never prevent best-draft delivery.
